01 · The challenge

A generation locked out of the classroom

Since 2021, girls in Afghanistan cannot attend school beyond grade 6. About 2.4 million girls are now excluded from secondary education. SOLA's own boarding school, relocated to Rwanda, received 5,385 applications in 2025 for 53 places. A physical campus could never meet this demand.

The brief

Deliver the national grade 7–12 curriculum plus ESL to girls at home, safely, on the cheapest possible technology, and at a scale of hundreds of thousands.

02 · My role

Turning the curriculum into micro-learning content

A separate analysis team ran the training needs analysis. My team at LearningMate took that TNA as our brief and turned textbook chapters into chat-ready micro-lessons.

Curriculum mapping

Broke each grade's textbook into units and single-objective modules, aligned to national standards.

Authoring

Wrote hooks, concept messages and worked examples in chat-sized chunks, using local, everyday contexts.

Assessment

Wrote tap-to-answer quick checks with feedback on each choice, plus unit quizzes.

Review and QA

Ran SME and language reviews across Dari, Pashto and English, and checked every module against a QA rubric.

My role: Lead Learning Designer, LearningMate Solutions

03 · Approach

From needs analysis to a lesson that fits a 6-minute gap

Each stage answered one question about the learner. Each answer became a design rule.

1 · DISCOVER

Training needs analysis

Run by the analysis team. Who learns, on what device, in what language, with how much time?

2 · DEFINE

Strategy and channel

Use WhatsApp over a native app. Self-paced micro-learning. Three languages.

3 · DESIGN

Module template

Hook, concept, example, check, reflect. One objective per module.

4 · DEVELOP

Content at scale

Curriculum mapping, authoring, translation and SME review, then QA.

5 · DELIVER

Launch and iterate

Launched March 2024. Data from the chatbot feeds content fixes.

04 · Training needs analysis

The brief we wrote content from

The analysis team's TNA looked at four areas. Each finding became a rule for how we wrote. The full TNA document has the tables, personas and evaluation plan.

Organization

Rigor without rote

SOLA wanted the national curriculum taught through inquiry, using National Geographic's Explorer Mindset framework, and free forever.

Learner

Borrowed phone, broken time

Most girls borrow a father's or brother's phone, have patchy internet, and get only short gaps between chores.

Task and content

Chapters are too big

A 45-minute textbook lesson had to be re-scoped into 5–8 minute modules, each with one objective and feedback written in.

Technology

Use the app they already have

WhatsApp is already on family phones, works on weak signal, needs no install, and looks like ordinary chat.

05 · Design principles

Six rules for learning on a shared phone

Chat first, nothing to install

Every lesson is a conversation in an app families already trust. No icon on the home screen gives a learner away.

Text first, media optional

Images and audio are small and can be skipped. A lesson still makes sense on a 2G signal.

One objective, six minutes

Modules fit the gap between chores. Pause anywhere; the bot remembers where you stopped.

Mother tongue by default

Learners choose Dari, Pashto or English and can switch mid-course. Right-to-left layouts are handled properly.

Tap, don't type

Numbered options and quick-reply buttons cut typing and errors for learners new to digital study.

Progress you can prove

Streaks, a progress bar and a certificate with a verifiable link replace the report card the ban took away.

Who we wrote for

A girl at home with a borrowed phone, a few quiet minutes, and every reason to keep learning.

Every module was checked against her: can she finish it in one sitting, on a weak signal, in her own language, without anyone needing to notice?

06 · Module anatomy

Every micro-lesson follows the same five beats

One template made authoring predictable for the content teams. It also made the rhythm familiar to learners.

~30s

Hook

A question from daily life

~2 min

Concept

Short text with an optional image or audio

~1 min

Example

A worked case using local context

~2 min

Quick check

2–3 tap answers with feedback on each

~30s

Reflect

One open "why" prompt

SOLAx LearningScience 8 · Why are leaves green?

HOOK

Think of a tree outside your home in summer, then in autumn. Why do the leaves change colour?

CONCEPT

Leaves contain chlorophyll. It absorbs red and blue light to make food, and reflects green light back to our eyes.

Listen in Dari · 0:48 · 180 KB

In autumn, the chlorophyll breaks down. Yellow and orange colours that were hidden all along start to show.

Without light, chlorophyll cannot make food. The plant uses up its stored energy, and its leaves turn pale and yellow.

08 · Outcomes

How the project succeeded

SOLAx passed its first-year reach goal and is now SOLA's largest program by far. The campus enrolls dozens of girls a year; SOLAx reaches tens of thousands.

Reach beyond the target

The goal was 10,000 learners by March 2025. By July 2025 SOLAx had more than 20,000 users in over 75 countries.

Access with no barriers

It is free, needs no application, and needs no install. Girls who were turned away by the campus can join the same day.

Strong partners

Meta provided WhatsApp API access. The National Geographic Society supported content development. SOLAx was recognized as an Echoing Green organization.

Credentials that count

Learners who pass a course get an instant certificate with a unique, verifiable URL. It gives them proof of learning when schools are closed.

Why it worked

Designed for real constraints. The channel, lesson length and media budget all came from the TNA, not from assumptions.

One template, many teams. A fixed module anatomy kept quality consistent across subjects, grades and three languages.

Safety as a feature. Studying looks like ordinary chat, which kept families comfortable and learners protected.

09 · Reflection

What I learned, and what comes next

Constraints make better design

Designing for a borrowed phone on a weak signal forced every word and image to justify itself. The lessons are clearer for it.

Next: personalized paths

SOLA is exploring generative AI for more tailored content. Adaptive practice and an AI study companion in Dari and Pashto are natural next steps.
